title: Design: the Status filter and its blue chip keep the columns in place
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts' and 'See Financial Data'.
  • Have a new matrix for this test, matrix A, pricing a new category made for this test.
  • Have a new matrix for this test, matrix B, which prices no category.
  • Use a desktop browser window exactly 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so the screen matches the design pictures' size.
custom_steps:
1. Click the Matrices tab on Settings › Pricing.
  2. Take a screenshot of the list.
  3. Open the Status filter.
  4. Pick Inactive.
  5. Close the filter panel.
  6. Take a second screenshot of the list.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The list shows matrix A (Active) and matrix B (Inactive).

Step 2:

  • The screenshot shows the list.

Step 3:

  • A panel opens under the Status chip with Active and Inactive, each with a checkbox and its count at the right, and a blue "Clear selection" link at the bottom, as in picture 6.5.

Step 4:

  • Inactive is ticked.

Step 5:

  • The chip turns blue and reads "Status: Inactive".
  • The label above the list counts the Inactive matrices; matrix B is listed and matrix A is hidden.

Step 6:

  • Compared with the first screenshot, the column headings Matrix, Status, Categories, Work Order Matrix, Part Sale Matrix and Tiers keep their places, as pictures 6.2 and 6.7 show.
  • The rows below the headings change to the Inactive matrices.
